item.title: PostgreSQL 18 Asynchronous IO Revolution: Why This Is the Biggest Database Update in 5 Years
item.description: PostgreSQL 18's asynchronous IO with io_uring delivers 3.4x faster sequential scans, 2.1x faster index scans. Real benchmark data, configuration guide, and migration strategy for the database performance revolution.

item.title: PostgreSQL Query Parsing Too Slow? PgDog Ditched Protobuf and Got 5x Faster
item.description: PgDog is a Rust-based PostgreSQL proxy. They discovered Protobuf serialization was the real bottleneck in SQL query parsing — not the Postgres parser itself. By replacing Protobuf with direct C-to-Rust FFI bindings, they achieved 5-10x faster parsing.

item.title: The C10M Problem in 2026: Why Your 128-Core Server Still Can't Handle 10 Million Packets Per Second
item.description: When packet rates surpass 2 million per second, the Linux network stack simply gives up. It's like your doorbell won't stop ringing, but you never have time to open the door. Let's talk about bypassing the kernel.

item.title: Manjaro 26.0 Is Here - Let's Talk About This Linux Distro
item.description: Manjaro 26.0 is officially released with KDE Plasma 6.5, Linux 6.18 kernel and more. Let's check out what's new in this beginner-friendly Arch-based distro.

item.title: gRPC is 10x Faster Than REST? Why Your Team Hasn't Switched
item.description: gRPC can indeed be much faster than REST, but most teams are right to stick with REST. Let's talk about the real cost behind the speed.

item.title: You Only Have Three Servers, Why Are You Using Kubernetes?
item.description: Kubernetes is for Google, systemd is for the rest of us. The story of someone who spent three months learning K8s, only to realize a single config file would have done the job.

item.title: The Linux Workflow That Doubled My Productivity: It's Not About Typing Faster
item.description: A few seemingly mundane Linux habits that doubled my daily development efficiency. The secret isn't typing faster—it's making fewer decisions.

item.title: European Governments Are Ditching Microsoft for Linux - What Do You Think of This Move?
item.description: Governments in Germany, Denmark, Spain and beyond are migrating from Windows to Linux at scale. This isn't a drill - it's really happening.
